violations.why: The ISR can write v_pebble between the two reads in the condition.
The ridge ISR enables hazel, which enables yarrow. Yarrow can then write v_ember between the task's two reads. v_cedar is 1 by then, so the write happens.
The summit ISR can preempt the task and write v_fjord between its two reads. v_harbor stays 1, so the write at line 48 happens.
The ISR can overwrite v_cedar between the read at line 69 and the read at line 30.
The ISR can change v_cedar between the check at line 30 and the argument read at line 32.
The ISR can read v_quartz between the task's two writes and see the intermediate value.
The ISR can read the v_vessel pointer between the task's two pointer writes.
The ISR can write v_meadow between the task's two reads.
The ISR increments v_pylon between the task's two index reads.
The ISR writes v_vessel[v_pylon] between the task's write and read-back, so the read can return the ISR's value.
When i is 2, the ISR overwrites v_vessel[2] between the task's write and its read-back.
The increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so the ISR's write can be lost.
Interrupt 1 is enabled at line 32. The basalt ISR can then write v_meadow between the two reads.
The vessel ISR preempts upland and enables interrupt 3. The nimbus ISR can then write v_amber between upland's two reads. v_jasper is 1 by then.
After enable_isr(1), the quiver ISR can increment v_umber between the task's check and its reset. The reset then overwrites the increment.
header and data overlap in the union. The ISR can read between the task's two writes and see a partial update.
The ISR can read v_umber between the task's two writes and see the intermediate value.
The ISR can write v_pylon between the check and the reset, and the reset then overwrites it.
The ISR can overwrite the zeroed v_pylon before the task reads it at line 30.
The ISR can change v_pylon between the task's two reads.
The ISR overwrites the freshly initialised loop counter before the loop condition reads it.
The ISR can change v_onyx between the loop check and its use as the array index.
The ISR can write v_onyx between the index read and the increment write, and the increment overwrites it.
The ISR can overwrite the incremented counter before the loop condition reads it.
The fjord ISR can write v_kestrel between the task's reads in the two functions.
The beacon ISR can write v_iris between the task's reads in the two functions.
The beacon ISR can write v_iris between the two reads in the area computation.
The task reads v_quiver[36] and later writes it back through v_ember. The ISR's write to v_quiver[36] in between is overwritten.
The ISR can overwrite v_vessel between the task's write and the later read.
The ISR can write v_vessel between the check and the update.
The ISR can write v_vessel between the check and the update.
The ISR can change v_vessel between the two reads that are copied to v_basalt.
The jasper ISR enables nimbus, which can write v_falcon between the task's two reads. v_hazel is 1 by then.
The nimbus ISR can write v_meadow between the task's two reads.
v_beacon[1] is read in both calls, and the ISR can clear it between the reads.
The meadow ISR can modify v_lantern between the check and the reset.
The meadow ISR enables nectar, which can modify v_lantern between the check and the reset.
The ISR can write v_quiver between the task's two reads.
After interrupt 1 is re-enabled at line 43, the ISR can write v_willow before the read at line 44.
After interrupt 1 is re-enabled at line 51, the ISR can write v_willow before the read at line 52.
The ISR reads v_vessel through v_tundra between the task's two writes and sees the intermediate value.
The ISR repoints v_timber at its own local before the task dereferences it.
The ISR can repoint v_timber between the task's two dereferences.
The ISR can reset v_fjord after the range check on the value read at line 12 but before the increment reads it.
The increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so the ISR's write can be lost.
The ISR can overwrite v_amber between the task's write and its first read.
The ISR can write v_amber between the task's consecutive reads.
The ISR can write v_amber between the task's consecutive reads.
The ISR can read v_glacier between the task's two writes and see the intermediate value. The write at line 27 is unreachable because v_meadow stays 0.
The higher-priority kelp ISR can overwrite v_fjord[TRIGGER] between the lantern ISR's write and its read.
The ISR overwrites v_glacier[40] between the task's write and its read-back.
After enable_isr(1), the walnut ISR can increment v_garnet between the task's check and its reset. The reset then overwrites the increment.
The zenith ISR enables indigo. Indigo can then read v_quartz[9999] between the task's two writes and see the intermediate value. v_willow is 1 by then.
Only interrupt 1 is masked, so the kestrel ISR can decrement v_basalt between the check and the reset.
The higher-priority kestrel ISR can preempt the willow ISR's read-modify-write of v_basalt.
